subject: Ceramics
examFormat: Three papers, all compulsory; Papers 1 and 2 are taken at one sitting. Paper 1: forty multiple-choice questions in 50 minutes for 40 marks. Paper 2: six essay-type questions, answer four, in 2 hours for 60 marks. Paper 3: two practical projects of which one is executed in five days at six hours per day for 80 marks; question papers are sent two weeks earlier and sketches and preparatory notes done in that period carry 20 marks, making 100 marks.
excluded: Names of Ghanaian indigenous pottery centres and Ghanaian pioneer ceramic artists listed under Ceramics as a Vocation (Ghana-specific).

topics.name: Ceramics as a Vocation
objectives: Define ceramics and describe its history
State career opportunities in ceramics
Identify types of products, e.g. bricks, tiles, vases, bowls, and their utilitarian and decorative uses
Relate ceramic products to the culture of the people
Describe indigenous pottery

topics.name: Raw Materials (Clay, Glazes and Other Raw Materials)

subtopics.name: Clay
objectives: Define clay and describe its formation, kinds and types, e.g. primary clay (kaolin), secondary clay (ball clay), earthenware clay, stoneware
Carry out prospecting and tests for clays: plasticity, shrinkage, firing temperature etc.
Prepare clay and identify types of clay bodies, e.g. plastic, rough
Identify sources of raw materials

subtopics.name: Glazes, colouring oxides, stains etc.
objectives: Identify glazes, colouring oxides, stains and other raw materials

subtopics.name: Tools
objectives: Identify ceramic tools, their uses and maintenance, e.g. modelling and trimming tools, sponge, cutting wire, callipers, knives, scraper, kidney, dipper

subtopics.name: Equipment
objectives: Identify ceramic equipment, its uses and maintenance, e.g. kilns, kiln furniture, potter's wheel, blunger, pug mill, jaw crusher, filter press, ball mill, dehumidifier, spraying booth, spraying machine, sackboard

subtopics.name: Design and construction of ceramic tools and equipment
objectives: Design and construct tools and equipment, e.g. forming tools, modelling tools, cutting wire, dipper, sackboard, rolling pin, kiln design and construction

subtopics.name: Drawing and designing
objectives: Develop ideas through sketching, drawing, dimension planning, computer aided designing etc.

subtopics.name: Hand building, wheel work and casting
objectives: Use hand building methods, e.g. pinching, coiling, slabbing
Use wheel work, e.g. throwing and turning
Use casting, pressing and extrusion

subtopics.name: Decorative processes
objectives: Use decorative processes, e.g. stamping, inlaying, incision, embossing, sgraffito, slip trailing, glazing, sprigging, spraying, painting, printing

subtopics.name: Drying and firing
objectives: Describe drying and firing: open firing, kiln firing (bisque firing) and glost firing

subtopics.name: Glazing
objectives: Describe glaze preparation, application, firing and its defects

subtopics.name: Factors in establishing a ceramic industry
objectives: Consider site finding, financing, branding, registration, licensing, labour and quality control

subtopics.name: Entrepreneurial skills
objectives: Manage a ceramic enterprise

subtopics.name: Costing, pricing, packaging and marketing of ceramic objects
objectives: Carry out market surveying and valuing
Consider labour cost, transportation etc. in costing, pricing, packaging and marketing

topics.name: Exhibition
objectives: Define exhibition and state its types
Plan and organize exhibitions

topics.name: Ceramic Production and Sustainable Environmental Issues
objectives: Address sustainable environmental issues in ceramic production: energy conservation, afforestation, land reclamation etc.

topics.name: Professional Practices and Ethics
objectives: Practise healthy studio practices
Build a portfolio of works
Develop a business plan
Prepare a brochure and business card
Develop a portfolio
Promote a sustainable environment

topics.name: Museum and Galleries
objectives: Define the museum and describe its history and development
State the functions and socio-economic importance of the museum
Describe the administrative structure of the museum
Explain the authenticity and neutrality of the museum
Give examples of museums and their activities
